# sugar/forin

> Loop over a slice or a string: for x in xs ... end

truck [sugar](../sugar.md) · [source](../../../registry/sugar/forin.pkg)

```
let primes = make([int], 3)
primes[0] = 2
primes[1] = 3
primes[2] = 5
for p in primes
  print p * p
end

for c in "hey"
  print c as int     // 104, 101, 121
end
```

`x` takes each element in turn: an element of a slice, or a byte (`u8`)
of a `str`. It only exists inside the loop, and assigning to it doesn't
change the slice. `break` and `continue` work as in any loop. `xs` is
evaluated once, before the first iteration:

```
do
  let xs_ = xs
  let i_ = 0
  while i_ < len(xs_)
    let x = xs_[i_]
    ...
  next
    i_ = i_ + 1
  end
end
```

## Syntax

Kind: `statement`; flags `loop`

```
for {x: newvar of xs[]} in {xs: expr [T]} {body: block} end
for {x: newvar of xs[]} in {xs: expr str} {body: block} end
```

| slot | takes | type |
|---|---|---|
| `x` | new variable name | type of `xs[]` |
| `xs` | expression | `[T]` |
| `body` | block of statements | — |
| `x` | new variable name | type of `xs[]` |
| `xs` | expression | `str` |
| `body` | block of statements | — |

## Expands to

This package has no backend: each use is rewritten to the following
source, with `{slot}` replaced by what was written there, and compiled again.

```
do
let {$xs} = {xs}
let {$i} = 0
while {$i} < len({$xs})
let {x} = {$xs}[{$i}]
{body}
next
{$i} = {$i} + 1
end
end
```
